topArticle.title: South African airline defends dramatic low-level flyby before rugby union clash
topArticle.description:
Cape Town stunt sparks major debate over safety risks

Airlink insists flyby conducted according to regulations

A pre-game stunt involving two passenger jets flying dramatically low over a stadium in South Africa drew huge cheers from the estimated crowd of 56,000 people, but also sparked a major debate over safety risks. The flyby by two Embraer jets, operated by the local airline Airlink, happened on Saturday before the second rugby union Test between South Africa and New Zealand in Cape Town.
The flight tracking service Flightradar24 estimated that the lead jet passed just 41-46 feet (12-14 metres) above the roof of Cape Town Stadium, with the crowd and the world’s top-ranked rugby teams below. The second jet, which was very close behind, flew through a cloud of pink dust that shot up from the stadium roof as part of the show.

topArticle.description:
Meanwhile, Trump posts video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign and replacing it with Lake America sign
Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel on Saturday over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting a video of him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA.
Rhetoric over the naming of Lake Ontario is the public face of an escalating trade dispute between the US and its northern neighbor involving a 50% US tariff on Canadian steel and retaliatory tariffs from Ottawa.

topArticle.description:
Pedro Sánchez says two countries cooperating and accuses Israel and Russia of spreading fake news about migration
Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has said there is no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta but accused Israel and Russia of spreading disinformation.
As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter the Spanish enclave at the end of July. The influx of about 70,000 men, women and children unleashed a political crisis, a humanitarian emergency and reignited tensions within the EU over immigration.

topArticle.title: People fleeing Sudan civil war face ‘dire and deteriorating’ conditions in refuge city
topArticle.description:
More traumatised civilians are arriving every day at ‘shockingly overcrowded’ El Obeid and camps on its outskirts
Humanitarian conditions in the Sudanese city of El Obeid and two camps on its outskirts are dire and deteriorating, according to people on the ground, as civilians displaced by fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia continue to pour in from the surrounding countryside.
The UN says more than 15,000 families have arrived since mid-July, joining more than 200,000 people who arrived in the first half of the year, according to government figures cited by Save the Children.

Police hunt two suspects after historic 200-carat piece is snatched from Austrian museum during opening hours
Austrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds that was on loan to a museum in Vienna and once belonged to Egyptian royalty.
Authorities in the capital released pictures of the suspects captured by security cameras during the heist at the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK), amid a rash of spectacular smash-and-grab thefts from European cultural institutions.

Reports that the US is preparing to claim a big stake in Venezuela’s massive energy reserves have sparked an outcry, with critics describing the move as “predatory” and a “rapacious” land grab.
Several media outlets this week reported that the Trump administration – which abducted Venezuela’s authoritarian president, Nicolás Maduro, in January and has steered the South American country ever since – hopes to secure long-term access to its oil and gasfields.

topArticle.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?
topArticle.description:
Fighters in legal limbo after accepting ‘total peace’ plan of Petro government just days before hardliner Abelardo De la Espriella took over
In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine guns and grenade launchers.
They also stripped off their heavy tactical vests, field packs and camouflage uniforms, which were each piled into a bonfire to mark the beginning of a new life away from an armed conflict that has claimed nearly half a million lives in the last six decades.

topArticle.summary: マルコ・ルビオ上院議員が発表した最新の制裁により、国際社会主義研究所とキューバ建設省が米国の制裁対象となった。

topArticle.title: Peru earthquake damages buildings and causes power cuts
topArticle.description: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck the Ayacucho region on Thursday, the US Geological Survey says.
topArticle.titleJa: ペルー地震で建物損壊、停電発生
topArticle.summary: 木曜日にアヤクチョ地域でマグニチュード6.7の地震が発生し、建物に被害を与え、広範囲で停電を引き起こしたと米国地質調査所が発表した。

topArticle.title: Panama Canal to cut number of ships passing through due to El Niño
topArticle.description: The crucial waterway's operator says low rainfall caused by the ocean pattern had led to the decision.
topArticle.titleJa: パナマ運河、エルニーニョ現象で通航船舶数を削減へ
topArticle.summary: エルニーニョ現象による降雨量不足のため、パナマ運河の運営当局は通航できる船舶数を削減すると発表。世界の貿易に影響を与える見込み。

topArticle.title: Livestreamer's murder raises questions over relations between Mexico's creators and cartels
topArticle.description: The murder of content creator César Gastélum on Tuesday raises questions about why influencers are coming under attack.

topArticle.summary: 火曜日にコンテンツクリエイターのセサル・ガステルム氏が殺害された事件は、メキシコでなぜインフルエンサーが攻撃されるのかという疑問を提起している。

topArticle.title: Amid political and economic pressure, Brazil sees a rise in land conflicts and the murders of Indigenous people
topArticle.description: Growing cases of violence against Indigenous people are linked to an impasse on the framework of rights and pressure against land demarcation, says the organization that advocates for Indigenous rights
topArticle.titleJa: 政治的・経済的圧力の中、ブラジルで土地紛争と先住民殺害が増加
topArticle.summary: 政治的・経済的圧力により、ブラジルで土地紛争が増え、先住民に対する暴力や殺害が増加している。これは権利の枠組みの行き詰まりと土地の区画分けに対する圧力に関連している。

topArticle.title: Weaponizing citizenship: Silencing dissent in Nicaragua
topArticle.description: In this edition, we examine an authoritarian narrative making the case for denationalization in Nicaragua.
topArticle.titleJa: 市民権の武器化：ニカラグアにおける反対意見の封殺
topArticle.summary: ニカラグアで、異議を唱える人々から市民権を剥奪する権威主義的な動きが、批判を抑え込むためにどのように利用されているかを検証する。

topArticle.title: Once a village, now barren land - BBC in valley devastated by floods
topArticle.description: The BBC reports from Sano Barkhu, a village overlooking the town of Syfrubesi, which was destroyed by the Nepal flooding.
topArticle.titleJa: 「かつて村、今は不毛の地」BBCが洪水で壊滅した渓谷から報道
topArticle.summary: ネパールを襲った洪水により、サノ・バルク村とシフルベシの町が壊滅状態となり、BBCが現地から被害を伝えている。

topArticle.title: Why is this teenager fighting fires dressed as Superman?
topArticle.description: A 17-year-old boy has gone viral for wearing a superhero costume while volunteer firefighting in Indonesia, as the country faces a super El Niño.
topArticle.titleJa: なぜこのティーンエイジャーはスーパーマンの格好で火災と戦っているのか？
topArticle.summary: インドネシアで大規模なエルニーニョ現象による火災が続く中、スーパーマンの衣装を着て消火活動を行う17歳の少年が話題になっている。

topArticle.title: 'Like fighting a dinosaur': Sydney woman recalls how she punched shark during attack
topArticle.description: Leah Stewart, 34, was mauled by a great white shark in June during a morning swim at Coogee Beach.
topArticle.titleJa: 「恐竜と戦うようだった」シドニーの女性がサメ襲撃時にパンチした体験を語る
topArticle.summary: 6月にクーギービーチでホホジロザメに襲われたシドニーの女性リア・スチュワートさん（34）が、サメにパンチした時の状況を語った。

topArticle.title: Wife of man who died after turbulence sues Singapore Airlines
topArticle.description: Lawyers for Linda Kitchen say her husband was "fatally injured" after the flight dropped 6,000 ft.
topArticle.titleJa: 乱気流後に死亡した男性の妻がシンガポール航空を提訴
topArticle.summary: 乱気流で夫が「致命的な負傷」を負い死亡したとして、リンダ・キッチン氏の弁護団がシンガポール航空を提訴した。

topArticle.title: Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour
topArticle.description: Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed says he and his players did not know about a Pakistan Cricket Board threat to the England and Wales Cricket Board over a Sky interview with the sons of Imran Khan.
topArticle.titleJa: サルファラーズ、パキスタンがツアー中止を脅迫したことを否定
topArticle.summary: パキスタン代表のサルファラーズ・アハメドヘッドコーチが、イムラン・カーン氏の息子たちのインタビューを巡るツアー中止の脅迫について、自身も選手も知らなかったと述べた。

topArticle.title: Madagascar launches safeguard investigation on self-adhesive labels, packaging and certain other printed items
topArticle.description: On 28 August 2026, Madagascar notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards that it had initiated on 13 August 2026 a safeguard investigation on imports of self-adhesive labels, packaging and other printed items on paper, cardboard, plastics, textiles or other similar materials.
topArticle.titleJa: マダガスカル、自己粘着性ラベル、包装材などの印刷物に対するセーフガード調査を開始
topArticle.summary: マダガスカルは、自己粘着性ラベルや包装材などの輸入品に対してセーフガード調査を開始したことをWTOに通知した。

topArticle.title: Lithuania gives EUR 30,000 to help developing economies and LDCs improve trade skillset
topArticle.description: Lithuania is contributing EUR 30,000 (approximately CHF 28,000) in 2026 to finance training programmes for government officials from developing economies, including least-developed countries (LDCs). This contribution to the WTO Global Trust Fund will support these economies in deepening their expertise on WTO issues and help them participate more effectively in the rules-based multilateral trading system.
topArticle.titleJa: リトアニア、開発途上国とLDCの貿易スキル向上に3万ユーロを拠出
topArticle.summary: リトアニアは、開発途上国やLDCの貿易スキル向上研修のため、WTOグローバル信託基金に3万ユーロを拠出した。

topArticle.title: Uzbekistan reaffirms 2026 WTO accession goal, thanks members for continuing engagement
topArticle.description: Uzbekistan reaffirmed its determination to complete its WTO accession process within 2026 at a meeting of the Working Party on the Accession of Uzbekistan on 27 and 28 July, soon after its last meeting in March. The head of Uzbekistan's delegation, Chief Negotiator Azizbek Urunov, stressed that maintaining a strong pace of engagement and addressing members' remaining concerns will be critical to bringing the accession process to a successful conclusion.
topArticle.titleJa: ウズベキスタン、2026年のWTO加盟目標を再確認、加盟国に継続的な関与に感謝
topArticle.summary: ウズベキスタンは、2026年中のWTO加盟プロセス完了への決意を再確認し、加盟国に対し継続的な関与への謝意を表明した。
